title: Proofreaders and Copy Markers
description: Read transcript or proof type setup to detect and mark for correction any grammatical, typographical, or compositional errors. Excludes workers whose primary duty is editing copy. Includes proofreaders of braille.
tasks: Mark copy to indicate and correct errors in type, arrangement, grammar, punctuation, or spelling, using standard printers' marks.
Read corrected copies or proofs to ensure that all corrections have been made.
Correct or record omissions, errors, or inconsistencies found.
Compare information or figures on one record against same data on other records, or with original copy, to detect errors.
Route proofs with marked corrections to authors, editors, typists, or typesetters for correction or reprinting.
Consult reference books or secure aid of readers to check references with rules of grammar and composition.
Consult with authors and editors regarding manuscript changes and suggestions.
Archive documents, conduct research, and read copy, using the internet and various computer programs.
Write original content, such as headlines, cutlines, captions, and cover copy.
Typeset and measure dimensions, spacing, and positioning of page elements, such as copy and illustrations, to verify conformance to specifications, using printer's ruler or layout software.
Read proof sheets aloud, calling out punctuation marks and spelling unusual words and proper names.

role_contexts.Face-to-Face Discussions with Individual: Once a week or more but not every day

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to catch what everyone else missed—to be the final barrier between error and permanence, because once something passes through their hands uncorrected, it becomes real forever.
psychological_profile.decision_style: Under uncertainty, they freeze and recheck rather than guess, defaulting to exhaustive comparison against reference materials until certainty is manufactured; when the clock ticks, they sacrifice speed for verification, often missing deadlines rather than shipping doubt.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They notice deviation before content—discrepancy, inconsistency, misalignment jumps out while meaning and intent fade to background; they prioritize the measurable over the arguable and instinctively dismiss subjective quality judgments as unverifiable noise.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is to document and escalate rather than confront directly, routing disagreement upward through proper channels; conflict carries the emotional cost of having their own precision questioned, which feels like an attack on their perceptual reliability.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: Risk-averse to the point of paralysis regarding any error that could propagate, but quietly risk-tolerant of bureaucratic friction, delays, and damaged relationships if those are the cost of certainty.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to invisible infrastructure—present but unacknowledged, neither leading nor following but standing adjacent to process, maintaining distance through transactional formality; when unassigned, they become the person who notices the thing no one asked them to check.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: Negotiation through rule-citation, treating hierarchy as a reference system to be consulted and leveraged rather than obeyed or subverted.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First emotional reaction is visceral shame at having been perceptually unreliable, followed by compulsive re-examination of their own prior work to locate systemic blind spots rather than external attribution.
value_hierarchy: verifiable correctness over diplomatic preservation of relationships
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate the detectability of errors through repetition, believing that checking something three times guarantees what checking it twice missed.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They need to be invisible to be effective—if their work is noticed, something has gone wrong—yet crave recognition for the disasters they alone prevented.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not normalize 'good enough' or sign off on known imperfections to meet deadlines, even under explicit pressure to do so.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: People who treat precision as pedantry, who say 'you know what I meant' and expect errors to be forgiven in the name of speed or creativity.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They reject the professional virtue of 'knowing when to let things go' or 'not sweating the small stuff,' considering it a license for carelessness dressed as wisdom.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: When things go wrong, they blame the upstream handoff—the person who created the error, not the system that allowed it through—believing errors have authors, not contexts.
